title: Applied ML Evals: Unified Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, Guardrails, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Applied ML guidance for onboarding models into the eval harness, creating and curating prompt sets and benchmarks, applying quantization profiles, establishing quality guardrails, and running regression triage. The goal is to provide a reproducible, auditable, and cross-functional process that keeps model serving quality high while enabling cost/performance optimizations.

Scope

- Model types: open and proprietary decoder-only and encoder-decoder LLMs used in Redwood inference pipelines.
- Workflows covered: model onboarding, baseline evaluation, prompt set curation, quantization validation, quality guardrails definition, and regression triage.
- Audience: Applied ML, Model Onboarding, Serving Runtime, SRE, and Product ML stakeholders.

Owner and Contacts

- Playbook owner: Applied ML (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Primary contacts: Applied ML (eval-harness), Eng Serving Runtime, Eng SRE
- Escalation path: On-call Applied ML -> Model Onboarding Lead -> Eng SRE -> Head of Serving Runtime

Key Definitions

- Eval harness: standardized test harness that runs prompt sets, collects metrics (accuracy, factuality, toxicity, latency, token-cost) and produces artifact bundles for review.
- Prompt set: curated collection of input-output pairs and scenario templates representative of customer workloads and edge cases.
- Quantization profile: configuration for weight/activation quantization and runtime parameters used to trade accuracy for cost/perf.
- Regression: any measurable drop in quality or change in distribution of eval metrics that exceeds defined thresholds.

High-level Process (summary)

1) Pre-onboarding: gather model metadata and artifacts.
2) Baseline eval: run eval harness with canonical prompt sets.
3) Quantization experiments: run quant profiles and compare deltas.
4) Guardrails definition: define thresholds and alert rules for production.
5) Deploy to canary: small traffic rollout with telemetry.
6) Regression triage: if metrics breach, run triage playbook.

1) Pre-onboarding checklist

- Required artifacts: model weights, model card (license, provenance), tokenizer, config (architecture, seq_len), example prompts.
- Metadata fields: model_name, version, training_data_summary, expected tokenization differences, recommended quantization profiles.
- Security review: confirm license compatibility and PII exposure assessment.
- Ownership and SLAs: assign owner_team, support_oncall, and expected SLOs for latency and availability.

2) Baseline evaluation (Eval Harness integration)

Purpose: produce a reproducible baseline of quality and performance before any optimization.

Steps:
1. Register model in the eval harness registry with the metadata above.
2. Select canonical prompt sets (see Prompt Set Guidelines below) and any workload-specific sets from product teams.
3. Run the full eval suite: accuracy/fact-checking, instruction-following, safety/toxicity, response-length distribution, latency and token cost distribution.
4. Produce an evaluation bundle (artifact) containing raw outputs, metric CSVs, diffs against reference model(s), and an evaluation summary PDF.
5. Store artifacts in the central eval artifacts S3 path: s3://redwood-evals/{model_name}/{version}/{date}/

Baseline metrics to capture (minimum):
- Instruction-following score (0-1)
- Factuality precision/recall (task dependent)
- Toxicity rate (percentage flagged by safety model)
- Average latency P50/P95 (ms) at standard request size
- Token cost per response (tokens_out + tokens_in) and per-request distribution

3) Prompt set creation and curation guidelines

- Principle: prompt sets should be representative, diverse, and reproducible. Prefer templated scenarios with variable placeholders to expand coverage.
- Categories: Core (canonical tasks), Product-specific (from integrators), Adversarial (targeted failure modes), Edge-cases (rare but high-impact queries), Localization (language/regional variants).
- Required metadata per prompt set: name, intent, generation-date, author, validation-method, expected-metric-impact, tags.
- Validation: each prompt set must include an acceptance threshold (e.g., baseline accuracy >= 0.85) and a held-out golden answers file.
- Versioning: store prompt sets in the prompt set catalog with semver-like versioning (v0.1.0).

Examples:
- Core/instruction-following: 2k templated instruction prompts across diverse intent categories.
- Adversarial: 200 targeted prompts designed to surface hallucination and information leakage.

4) Quantization profiles and validation

Purpose: reduce serving cost without unacceptable quality regression.

Workflow:
1. Identify candidate profiles: {fp16, int8_dynamic, int8_static, awq, gptq} with parameterizations.
2. For each profile, run the quantization pipeline to produce quantized model artifacts.
3. Run the same eval harness suite used in baseline. Capture delta metrics and per-prompt diffs.
4. Evaluate performance (latency P50/P95, memory usage, throughput) on representative hardware (e.g., A100-80GB, H100, T4).
5. Create a quantization evaluation matrix: profile, size reduction, latency delta, instruction-following delta, factuality delta, safety delta.

Acceptance criteria for promoting a quantized variant:
- Instruction-following delta >= -0.02 (relative) AND factuality delta within acceptable band (task-specific)
- No new safety/toxicity regressions above baseline tolerance (e.g., +0.5% absolute)
- Throughput/latency improvement justifies cost delta per token

Documentation: each promoted profile must include the profile YAML, validation artifacts, and recommended runtime flags.

5) Quality guardrails (prod monitoring and alerts)

Key metrics to monitor in production:
- User-facing quality: instruction-following score (sampled), hallucination/factuality flags, safety/toxicity flags.
- Performance: P50/P95 latency, error rate (5xx + model-runtime-errors), throughput per instance.
- Cost signals: average tokens per request, cache hit rate, batching efficiency.

Guardrail thresholds (examples):
- Instruction-following rolling 24h mean drops by >3% relative to baseline -> create alert (SEV3).
- Factuality regression: +2% absolute increase in hallucination flags -> SEV2.
- Safety/toxicity: any day with >0.5% high-severity safety flags -> SEV1 and immediate rollback consideration.
- Latency increase: P95 latency increases by 40% -> SEV2.

Alert actions (automated where possible):
1. Notify on-call Applied ML and Product owner.
2. If safety SEV1, trigger immediate partial rollback to last-known-good model variant.
3. Capture 1,000 recent request/response samples and attach to a triage ticket.

6) Regression triage playbook (runbook)

Trigger: any alert emitted by guardrails or customer-reported quality incident.

First responders: Applied ML on-call and Model Onboarding lead.

Triage steps (numbered):
1. Triage intake: collect incident ticket, alert graphs, and the evaluation artifact for the currently promoted variant.
2. Scope classification: is the regression systemic (all traffic) or scoped to a subset (route, prompt-set, locale)?
   - Use request sampling and metadata (model_version, route, region, user_agent) to filter.
3. Reproduce locally: run the eval harness against the production model variant using the implicated prompt sets and sampled requests.
4. Compare to baseline artifacts: compute per-prompt diffs, identify clustered failure modes (e.g., hallucination on finance prompts).
5. Hypothesis generation: common causes include quantization side-effects, tokenizer changes, recent prompt engineering, rollout variant mismatch, or data drift.
6. Mitigations (prioritized):
   a. Immediate rollback to last-known-good variant (if large-scale or safety issue).
   b. If limited scope, update routing policy to route affected subset to safer variant.
   c. Introduce a quick fix in preprocessing (e.g., tokenization normalization) if applicable.
   d. If caused by quantization, switch to a higher-precision profile for the model in question.
7. Post-mortem: document root cause, steps taken, timeline, and preventive changes to tests or guardrails.

Triage output artifacts:
- Triage ticket with timeline and owner.
- Repro script and minimal failing prompt set.
- Suggested long-term fixes and prioritization.

7) Automation and CI integration

- Evaluation runs must be automated in CI for pull requests touching model code or quantization configs.
- Key checks (blocking): instruction-following delta <= -0.02, safety delta <= 0.005 absolute, and no new high-severity safety flags in the top-200 prompts.
- Nightly regression suite: run a full eval against production variants and compare to previous 7-day baseline; open tickets for any threshold breaches.

8) Dashboards and observability

Recommended dashboards to create in Grafana/Looker:
- Model health overview (per-variant): instruction-following, factuality, toxicity, latency P50/P95, token cost trends.
- Prompt-set failure heatmap: rows=prompt-categories, cols=time, color=delta from baseline.
- Quantization comparison dashboard: toggle between profiles and show metric deltas.

Instrumentation requirements:
- Attach model_version, quant_profile, prompt_set_id, route, region, and request_id to traces.
- Sample 1% of requests for full output storage (rotated) and 100% for safety-suspect flags.

9) Rollout checklist (canary and promote)

- Canary (0-5% traffic for 24-72 hours): monitor guardrails every 1 hour and run targeted evals every 6 hours.
- Gradual promote (5->25->50->100%): hold at each step for a minimum of 12 hours and validate metrics.
- Automatic abort: any SEV1 safety trigger or >3% instruction-following drop relative to baseline -> rollback.

10) Post-incident and continuous improvement

- Postmortem must be written within 5 business days with a remediation plan and owner for each action item.
- Maintain a triage-runbook playbook page with canonical failing prompts for common categories (hallucination, refusal, safety).
- Quarterly review: audit prompt set coverage, update core canonical prompt sets, and rebaseline top customer workloads.

Appendices

A. Example CLI commands
- Run eval harness locally: ./eval_harness/run.py --model s3://models/modelX/v1 --prompt-set core-instructions-v1 --out artifacts/modelX_v1_eval
- Run quantization experiment: ./quantize/run_quant.py --model modelX --profile awq-8bit --out artifacts/modelX_v1_awq

B. Minimum artifact manifest (required for promotion)
- eval_summary.pdf
- raw_outputs.jsonl (sampled)
- metrics.csv
- quant_profile.yaml (if applicable)
- performance_bench.csv

C. Ownership matrix (examples)
- Eval harness infra: Applied ML infra team
- Prompt set catalog: Applied ML content owners + Product ML reviewers
- Production guardrails: Eng SRE + Applied ML

D. Related pages and templates
- Prompt set template (link): /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/prompt-set-template
- Eval artifact upload checklist: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/artifact-upload-guidelines

Contact and feedback

For questions or to request new prompt set support, file a ticket in the Applied ML backlog and tag @applied-ml. For urgent incidents, follow the on-call escalation path above.
summary: Unified playbook for onboarding models into the eval harness, creating/caring for prompt sets, validating quantization profiles, setting production guardrails, and executing regression triage.
